newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Dogs bark for democracy in Serbia.
newsitem.headline: Dogs bark for democracy in Serbia.

text.p: Dogs barked for democracy in Serbia on Sunday, joining their masters in a 63rd straight day of colourful street protests against the annulment of opposition victories in municipal elections.

Opposition activists trotted out their bulldogs, poodles, cocker spaniels, Irish setters, rotweilers, dalmatians, great danes, chihuahuas and so on to add canine cacophony to the usual din of whistles, drums and chants.
Some of the pooches looked flustered from all the noise but others joined in heartily, barking in unison at cordons of riot police set up to enforce a ban on street marches.
People without live dogs carried cuddly toy animals. One woman cuddled a mouse, while a man had a pink panther.
The nine weeks of demonstrations by Serbia's Zajedno (Together) coalition have been distinctive for their non-violence, creativity and humour, and Sunday's rally of the dogs was no exception.
Zajedno leaders had urged their faithful to "walk your dogs" on Sunday, a day after protesters dressed up in uniforms to mock the riot police who shadow them every day.
"They have banned our walks. They say the president (Slobodan Milosevic) thinks our walks are bad for our health," Zajedno co-leader Zoran Djindjic said on Saturday.
"But does our president like our dogs to walk? At 3 p.m. tomorrow, take out your dogs and let's see if they will be permitted to walk. And if you don't have a dog bring something else, maybe a duck."
Some 30,000 demonstrators in Belgrade on Saturday wore army fatigues, hospital garb, hockey kits and a motley array of other uniforms.
Zajedno is trying to force Milosevic's government to accept that opposition won control of 14 of Serbia 18 largest cities including Belgrade in November elections.
Milosevic and his Socialist Party have so far resisted international pressure to recognise the results.
